impact: The two Codex real-client cells ran with userConfigIsolated:false and were published as unqualified passes. `codex exec -c` has no equivalent of Claude Code's --strict-mcp-config plus --settings, so the operator's own ~/.codex configuration was reachable during those runs: they establish that the SDK works on this machine, not from a fresh state. Confirmed independently by the reviewer at major severity in both chunk 17b (manifests) and chunk 17c (receipt). PARTIALLY ADDRESSED in commit 5aa951b: verify-evidence now shape-checks manifest.isolation, collects a typed qualification per unisolated cell, and both DECISION.md and decision.json carry it, so nothing downstream can read an unconditional pass any more; a hostile config that actually executed is now a hard refusal rather than a qualification. DEFERRED REMAINDER: marking the two cells not-run and recapturing under an isolated temporary CODEX_HOME, which is what would actually close the gap. That requires copying authentication material into a temporary home, and this project's standing constraints forbid modifying ~/.codex/config.toml and forbid copying credentials, so it cannot be done autonomously — it is an owner decision about whether to relax that constraint or accept the qualified evidence.
resolution:
Resolved across c3a7170, 9406536 and fad6719.

Isolation is now a GATE, not a footnote. A cell whose manifest does not record userConfigIsolated publishes as `not-run` with a stated cause instead of a qualified `pass`, so it cannot contribute to an adoption; not-run dominates, so evidence containing one reaches no verdict at all. Previously such a cell counted as a mandatory pass and the shortfall was demoted to DECISION.md prose, which is not a gate.

The premise underneath the issue turned out to be false, and that is the more useful half of this. The suspicion was that Codex could not be isolated and that its cells were therefore passing on the operator's own configuration. The first claim was wrong — `codex exec --ignore-user-config` exists on codex-cli 0.144.0 and its own help text separates config from auth — and it was wrong in the code too: capture.mjs hardcoded `userConfigIsolated: client === "claude-code"`, so every Codex capture was born unisolated regardless of how it actually ran. Left uncorrected, the new gate would have made every Codex cell permanently not-run and forced an owner decision (drop Codex from the mandatory set, or accept non-isolated evidence) that was manufactured entirely by an unchecked factual claim.

The second claim was right, and isolating Codex is what proved it. With the operator's ~/.codex/config.toml excluded, both Codex cells failed — the client cancelled its own tool call because nothing remained that approved the server. The earlier passes had been leaning on that file's per-project trust entries. So those cells were only ever passes on this machine, exactly as suspected, and it took genuine isolation to demonstrate rather than argue it. Filed as ISS-055, since it is a property of the client and reaches users.

Enforcement rather than prose, in each direction:
- CAN_ISOLATE_USER_CONFIG is a pinned literal per client, backed by a NAMED mechanism, not a claim a manifest makes about itself.
- capture.mjs preflights the isolation flags against the installed binary and runs a malformed-config differential witness before any quota is spent; a client that cannot isolate yields `isolation-unavailable` rather than a silent unisolated capture.
- Tests assert the downgrade fires, that it is applied to the PUBLISHED cell after every validation step (so declaring yourself unisolated is not a way to skip checks), and that a downgraded cell carries no qualification describing it as a qualified pass.

All four real cells now pass under demonstrated isolation and every committed manifest records userConfigIsolated: true.
